items.summary: CrowdStrike says it uncovered personal details of a suspected 26-year-old in China's Guangdong province while analyzing AI coding-tool sessions and infrastructure tied to late-September attacks on South Korean banks. The actor used a Chinese open-source pentesting agent called ARTEX alongside large language models; attribution is made with moderate confidence.
items.title: CrowdStrike: China-based suspect used AI tools in South Korean bank hacks

items.summary: ASOS said Thursday that the breach earlier this week exposed some customers' personal information, including names and contact details, after hackers impersonated a trusted contact to steal an employee's login. No payment card data or account passwords were accessed; Snowflake said its platform was not breached.
items.title: ASOS confirms breach exposed some customer personal data

items.summary: Switzerland's federal pension fund Publica said it was exposed to a data leak after an external software provider suffered a cyberattack at the end of September. The provider was not identified; the Swiss Attorney General's office has opened an investigation.
items.title: Swiss pension fund hit by data leak after software provider cyberattack

items.summary: Japanese chip-testing giant Advantest confirmed that personal information — including SSNs, passport and driver's license numbers, plus medical and financial data — was stolen in the February ransomware attack it first disclosed earlier this year. The company has not said how many individuals are affected.
items.title: Advantest confirms personal data stolen in February ransomware attack

items.summary: A German-led international operation seized KillSec's data leak site, five servers and 110 terabytes of stolen data, with three arrests across Europe. Europol says a 16-year-old is believed to be the group's administrator; the group is linked to roughly 1,000 suspected attacks worldwide.
items.title: Law enforcement dismantles KillSec ransomware group in Operation KillSwitch

items.summary: Danish authorities disclosed that attackers exploited a legitimate company account to pull names, addresses and CPR numbers for about 8.8 million individuals from the Central Person Register over 10 days in September. The compromised account has been suspended and the Data Protection Agency notified.
items.title: Denmark's national register breach exposed data of 8.8 million people
